title: Bear and Tree Jumps
statementMd:
A tree is an undirected connected graph without cycles. The distance between two vertices is the number of edges in a simple path between them.

Limak is a little polar bear. He lives in a tree that consists of $*n*$ vertices, numbered $1$ through $*n*$.

Limak recently learned how to jump. He can jump from a vertex to any vertex within distance at most $*k*$.

For a pair of vertices $(*s*, *t*)$ we define $*f*(*s*, *t*)$ as the minimum number of jumps Limak needs to get from $*s*$ to $*t*$. Your task is to find the sum of $*f*(*s*, *t*)$ over all pairs of vertices $(*s*, *t*)$ such that $*s* < *t*$.

## Input

The first line of the input contains two integers $*n*$ and $*k*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 200 000$, $1 ≤ *k* ≤ 5$) — the number of vertices in the tree and the maximum allowed jump distance respectively.

The next $*n* - 1$ lines describe edges in the tree. The $*i*$-th of those lines contains two integers $*a*_{*i*}$ and $*b*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$) — the indices on vertices connected with $*i*$-th edge.

It's guaranteed that the given edges form a tree.

## Output

Print one integer, denoting the sum of $*f*(*s*, *t*)$ over all pairs of vertices $(*s*, *t*)$ such that $*s* < *t*$.

## Note

In the first sample, the given tree has $6$ vertices and it's displayed on the drawing below. Limak can jump to any vertex within distance at most $2$. For example, from the vertex $5$ he can jump to any of vertices: $1$, $2$ and $4$ (well, he can also jump to the vertex $5$ itself).

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2f64f096f9b26ecb178744d255b0b317185ae82b.png)

There are ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c0295201207e28a36e641d8cf599f45986059e71.png) pairs of vertices $(*s*, *t*)$ such that $*s* < *t*$. For $5$ of those pairs Limak would need two jumps: $(1, 6), (3, 4), (3, 5), (3, 6), (5, 6)$. For other $10$ pairs one jump is enough. So, the answer is $5·2 + 10·1 = 20$.

In the third sample, Limak can jump between every two vertices directly. There are $3$ pairs of vertices $(*s* < *t*)$, so the answer is $3·1 = 3$.
statementZhMd:
树是一种无向连通且无环的图。两个顶点之间的距离是它们之间一条简单路径所包含的边数。

Limak 是一只小北极熊。他生活在一棵由 $*n*$ 个顶点组成的树上，这些顶点编号为 $1$ 至 $*n*$。

Limak 最近学会了跳跃。他可以从一个顶点跳到距离不超过 $*k*$ 的任意顶点。

对于一对顶点 $(*s*, *t*)$，我们定义 $*f*(*s*, *t*)$ 为 Limak 从 $*s*$ 到 $*t*$ 所需的最少跳跃次数。你的任务是求满足 $*s* < *t*$ 的所有顶点对 $(*s*, *t*)$ 的 $*f*(*s*, *t*)$ 之和。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*k*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 200 000$，$1 ≤ *k* ≤ 5$）——树中的顶点数以及允许的最大跳跃距离。

接下来的 $*n* - 1$ 行描述树中的边。其中第 $*i*$ 行包含两个整数 $*a*_{*i}$ 和 $*b*_{*i}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i}$，$*b*_{*i}$ ≤ *n*$）——第 $*i*$ 条边所连接的顶点编号。

保证给出的边构成一棵树。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数，表示满足 $*s* < *t*$ 的所有顶点对 $(*s*, *t*)$ 的 $*f*(*s*, *t*)$ 之和。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，给出的树有 $6$ 个顶点，其结构如下图所示。Limak 可以跳到距离不超过 $2$ 的任意顶点。例如，从顶点 $5$ 出发，他可以跳到顶点 $1$、$2$ 和 $4$ 中的任意一个（当然，他也可以跳到顶点 $5$ 自身）。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2f64f096f9b26ecb178744d255b0b317185ae82b.png)

满足 $(*s*, *t*)$ 且 $*s* < *t*$ 的顶点对共有 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c0295201207e28a36e641d8cf599f45986059e71.png) 个。其中有 $5$ 对顶点需要跳跃两次：$(1, 6)$、$(3, 4)$、$(3, 5)$、$(3, 6)$、$(5, 6)$。其他 $10$ 对顶点跳跃一次即可。因此，答案为 $5·2 + 10·1 = 20$。

在第三个样例中，Limak 可以直接在任意两个顶点之间跳跃。满足 $*s* < *t*$ 的顶点对共有 $3$ 个，因此答案为 $3·1 = 3$。
